challenges.title: The midday work ban at uncovered terminals

items.title: The ban on outdoor work
items.text: From 15 June to 15 September, work in direct sunlight is banned every day from 12:30 to 15:00 — this also applies to loading and unloading staff at uncovered container terminals and loading yards (MOHRE ministerial decision).

items.title: Fines of up to AED 50,000 per breach
items.text: Breaches cost AED 5,000 per affected employee, capped at AED 50,000 — the same structure as the general midday work ban.

items.title: Distinguishing covered from uncovered areas
items.text: Only work in direct sunlight is affected — whether a loading area counts as covered or uncovered must be clearly documented for every shift.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off logistics operators in the UAE
solutions.subtitle: From the automatic block to covered/uncovered declarations — everything works together.

items.title: The midday window for outdoor shifts blocked automatically
items.text: Klacks automatically blocks open-air terminal and loading-yard shifts between 12:30 and 15:00 from 15 June to 15 September — every year, with no need to re-enter the dates by hand.

items.title: Covered or uncovered, clearly declared
items.text: Klacks lets you declare each terminal zone as covered or uncovered — only affected areas are blocked during the banned window.

items.title: The AED 50,000 fine risk avoided
items.text: Because the banned window can never be scheduled for outdoor areas in the first place, the risk of the AED 5,000 fine per employee simply doesn't arise.

items.title: Routes & deliveries automatically optimised
items.text: Klacks automatically aligns deliveries, loading times and staff deployment at the terminal.

items.title: On-premise: full data sovereignty
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure — your terminal team's personal data never leaves your organisation.

items.title: Klacksy schedules by voice
items.text: "Move the loading shift at Terminal 2 out of the midday window" is all it takes — Klacksy automatically observes the ban.

example.title: The midday ban at the terminal, at a glance
example.text: Klacks automatically recognises when a loading shift at an uncovered terminal between 15 June and 15 September falls within the banned window of 12:30 to 15:00, and moves it to the morning or late afternoon — no manual recalculating required.
